codeReview.summary: This fix resolves the prior blocking defect. `handleGitHubStatusCommand()` now returns success only when the emitted GitHub readiness payload is actually `ready: true`, so repo-bound status exit semantics match the shipped readiness contract instead of treating resolved profile/token state as sufficient. The added regression smokes in `tests/github-commands.test.ts` cover both the previously broken unhealthy app-profile case and the healthy ready path, and the existing readiness-payload coverage still exercises shared-scope-denied states.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The shared user-testing library still describes GitHub CLI validation as requiring a temporary global-config overlay because the project config only enables Linear and tickets, but the project config now enables `dance.hack.github`. That note is stale and can mislead later workers or validators about the current repo-bound GitHub setup.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: .factory/library/user-testing.md:15 states the project config only enables `dance.hack.linear` and `dance.hack.tickets`, while `.hack/hack.config.json:7-13` now includes `dance.hack.github` as an enabled extension.

summary: Pass. I reviewed the original failed feature and the follow-up fix together, including both handoffs, both transcript skeletons, the prior fail report, and the relevant commit diffs. The original blocking issue is fixed: repo-bound `github status` now exits according to `payload.ready`, so unhealthy readiness states no longer slip through as exit 0. I did not find new blocking or non-blocking code issues in the fix; the only follow-up I noted is a stale GitHub validation note in `.factory/library/user-testing.md`.
